notes.text: Teradata session mode: character comparisons are NOT CASESPECIFIC and ignore trailing pad spaces (leading spaces still count). DuckDB compares exactly. Applied as a general rule to every string comparison/IN/join in the estate: upper(rtrim(col,' ')) = upper(rtrim(literal,' ')). Applies to seg_filter (g01,g11,g14,g17,g19), status_counts (g02,g31), channel_revenue (g03,g16,g21,g26,g30), category_lines (g04,g24,g27,g28: category filter AND CHAR(10) sku join), and all dep_* status filters.

Case folding uses DuckDB upper() (Unicode). This matches Teradata for ASCII/LATIN data; non-Latin characters could compare differently. Only spaces count as pad characters (rtrim(x,' ')), so tabs or other whitespace still make values differ, as in Teradata.
Segment filter uses the case-insensitive, trailing-space-insensitive comparison rule generically; TRIM semantics identical.
Rule applied to every IN-list element; NULL status falls to ELSE 0 as in legacy.
Channel filter uses generic comparison rule.

order_lines.sku is CHAR(10) with trailing pad spaces while products.sku is VARCHAR without. In Teradata the join matches after padding; in DuckDB it would match nothing. Join is on upper(rtrim(sku,' ')) on both sides (same in g24,g27,g28).
Rule applied both to the CHAR(10) sku join (both sides) and the category filter.

RoundHalfwayMagUp=FALSE: Teradata CAST to DECIMAL with fewer scale digits rounds exact halves to even; DuckDB CAST rounds half away from zero. Converted as CAST(round_even(x,1) AS DECIMAL(14,1)) in all rounding scripts (g05,g12,g13,g15,g20,g25) and the amount_1dp column of all lines_by_status scripts (g35-g37,g39,g40,g44,g45); g42/g46 inherit it via value_1dp_20/value_1dp_05.
Half-even rounding via round_even before DECIMAL(14,1) cast (RoundHalfwayMagUp=FALSE).
TOP n WITH TIES has no DuckDB equivalent: converted to RANK() OVER (ORDER BY metric DESC NULLS LAST) <= n (Teradata sorts NULL as lowest, i.e. last in DESC). Same in g22,g23,g29,g42,g46.
TOP WITH TIES -> RANK()<=n with NULLS LAST in DESC.
ZEROIFNULL is not a DuckDB function: converted to COALESCE(x, 0) (same in g18).
COALESCE(x,0) keeps DECIMAL(12,2) type.
Teradata INTEGER/INTEGER truncates toward zero; DuckDB '/' returns DOUBLE. Converted to '//' (verified truncating toward zero: -7//2 = -3).
items_per_order uses integer division, so the fractional part is dropped (e.g. 7 items / 2 orders = 3). Reproduced for parity.
Integer division via // (truncation toward zero verified, including negative operands).
Teradata sorts NULLs first in ASC; DuckDB defaults NULLS LAST. Made explicit: ORDER BY ship_date ASC NULLS FIRST, order_id ASC NULLS FIRST.
'First order in fulfilment order' picks an unshipped order (NULL ship_date) ahead of any shipped one because of Teradata NULL ordering, which is probably not what was meant. Reproduced for parity.
Explicit NULLS FIRST on all ASC keys reproduces Teradata ordering.
DATE - DATE yields integer days in both engines; cast to INTEGER to match Teradata type. The CROSS JOIN to etl_control is kept as is (it assumes etl_control has one row).
Date difference in integer days; semantics identical.
